criteria.name: Task Response
criteria.essay_quote: Governments have to decide how to divide transport budgets between public services and roads.
criteria.title: Make each main idea do more work.
criteria.next_step: State a claim, explain why it follows, and add one relevant example.

example.after: Affordable buses can widen access to jobs because workers can reach employers beyond walking distance; for example, a low-cost commuter pass can connect outer suburbs to the city.
example.type: illustrative example, not an automatic correction of your text

rubric.text:
IELTS Academic Writing Task 2 | Task Response | Band 7
The main parts of the prompt are appropriately addressed.
A clear and developed position is presented.
Main ideas are extended and supported but there may be a
tendency to over-generalise or there may be a lack of focus and
precision in supporting ideas/material.

criteria.name: Coherence and Cohesion
criteria.essay_quote: I believe that public transport should receive greater investment in cities, although maintaining safe roads remains necessary.
criteria.title: Give each paragraph one clear purpose.
criteria.next_step: Use a topic sentence, develop that point, and make the connection to the next paragraph explicit.

example.before: It is cheap. Pollution is a problem.
example.after: Alongside lower travel costs, reliable public transport can reduce pollution by replacing some journeys made in private cars.
example.type: illustrative example, not an automatic correction of your text

rubric.text:
IELTS Academic Writing Task 2 | Coherence and Cohesion | Band 7
Information and ideas are logically organised,
and there is a clear progression throughout
the response. (A few lapses may occur, but
these are minor.)
A range of cohesive devices including
reference and substitution is used flexibly but
with some inaccuracies or some over/under
use.
Paragraphing is generally used effectively to
support overall coherence, and the sequencing
of ideas within a paragraph is generally logical.

criteria.name: Lexical Resource
criteria.essay_quote: A balanced policy can improve access to work while meeting the needs of people who cannot use a bus or train.
criteria.title: Choose precise words for your meaning.
criteria.next_step: Replace broad words with accurate topic vocabulary and check the surrounding word combination.

example.after: Two potential benefits are lower commuting costs and wider access to employment.
example.type: illustrative example, not an automatic correction of your text

rubric.text:
IELTS Academic Writing Task 2 | Lexical Resource | Band 7
The resource is sufficient to allow some
flexibility and precision.
There is some ability to use less common
and/or idiomatic items.
An awareness of style and collocation is
evident, though inappropriacies occur.
There are only a few errors in spelling
and/or word formation and they do not
detract from overall clarity.

criteria.name: Grammatical Range and Accuracy
criteria.essay_quote: The main reason to prioritize public transport is affordability.
criteria.title: Use sentence variety with control.
criteria.next_step: Combine two related ideas with a clear subordinate clause, then check agreement and punctuation.

example.before: Buses are cheap. People can use them.
example.after: Because buses are affordable, more residents can use them for daily travel.
example.type: illustrative example, not an automatic correction of your text

rubric.text:
IELTS Academic Writing Task 2 | Grammatical Range and Accuracy | Band 7
A variety of complex structures is used
with some flexibility and accuracy.
Grammar and punctuation are generally
well controlled, and error-free sentences
are frequent.
A few errors in grammar may persist, but
these do not impede communication.
